title: System Control Board: rows and details laid out like Jason's example
why: Jason, 2026-11-18, with a screenshot of a row from an example board: 'this example has a much better setup for the information. please address your layouts.' Each process row is now in columns, as his example: its mark; its name with the line under it (a workflow's phases, 0164 §7); its stage as a pill (Observation; Standby when it's switched on while the system is stopped; Holding; Shut down; Pre-flight); where it stands in a few words (what holds it, else why it's off, with 'n of m needs answered'); its last 24 hours (runs, and records in with how much is accounted for); its speed per record; its OK rate (calls without a server error, runs without a failure); and Check, Start or Shut down on the row itself (a button there doesn't open or close the row). The columns line up across rows. Opened, a row shows short labelled lines, label and value on one line: Route; Its check in one line, what holds it first, its parts on a toggle; Needs as chips ('Places by kind and town ✓ (our OpenStreetMap copy)'), every source in order on hover, a press tests that need; Accounting ('Received = Stored + Updated + To Review + Refused'); Runs; Dry run; Records touched lately; then its buttons. The site's own needs use the same chips. On a phone the row stacks, and an empty metric isn't shown. From his example, not here: Log and Report on each row (the logbook and reports are release 5), cost per record and uptime (release 4); the OK rate stands in for uptime until then. Built on Sync 17:14 UTC, after #928 went live. Tests: r2d.php 9 (the row's stage and hold, the check's line and toggle); rendered at 390px and 1280px with no sideways scroll; the row's Check and a need chip pressed. No tables or migrations. FAQ: the board's entry updated.
